theorem.statement:
The six-part request in \(\mathrm{oeq{:}generic\text{-}strict\text{-}containment}\) has a negative answer: its exceptional-equality-locus requirement is false even away from rank-degenerate respondent blocks and reward-history-blind deployment policies. More precisely, under the corrected full-history logging equation there is an exact rational slice with \(H=2\), \(\mathcal S_2=\mathcal S_3=\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), and \(\mathcal R=\{0,1,2\}\) whose full compatible fiber is the box-affine family \(q=q^0+B(\lambda_0,\lambda_1)^\top\), \((\lambda_0,\lambda_1)\in[0,2]^2\), displayed in the proof. On the deployment-policy coordinates \(x_r=\pi_2(1\mid R_1=r)\in(0,1)\), put
\[
M_7(x)=-x_0+3x_1-2x_2.
\]
Both rectangular endpoint inequalities are strict exactly when \(M_7(x)>0\), whereas both are equalities when \(M_7(x)\leq0\). The respondent matrix has rank two, and reward-history blindness is only the diagonal \(x_0=x_1=x_2\). Therefore, after those exceptional faces are removed, the equality locus contains a nonempty relatively open policy set and its complement also contains a nonempty relatively open policy set. It cannot be the compatible part of the common-zero variety of any finite polynomial family \(M_j\). At
\[
(x_0,x_1,x_2)=\left(\frac1{140},\frac{521}{980},\frac1{980}\right)
\]
the exact sharp image is \(\Theta_I(p)=[229/140,26/15]\), while \(L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=617/420\), \(U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=19/10\), and \(\Delta^-(p)=\Delta^+(p)=1/6\).
theorem.proof_tex:
We give a cell-complete rational construction and then eliminate its two latent coordinates. The technique is direct finite-table algebra, followed by an elementary polynomial-identity argument. This simultaneously checks that strict containment is real and proves that the requested algebraic characterization of all equality cases cannot be true.

Fix \(H=2\), \(S_1=s_0\), \(\mathcal S_2=\mathcal S_3=\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), and \(\mathcal R=\{0,1,2\}\). Let the behavior policy be
\[
\mu_1(a_1\mid s_0)=\frac12,
\qquad
\mu_2(a_2\mid h_2^O)=\frac12
\tag{1}
\]
for every action and every recorded history. Thus \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}positivity}\) holds with \(\epsilon=1/2\). Define
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}
1/12&1/12&0\\
0&1/6&1/12
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\boldsymbol\beta=\begin{pmatrix}1/4\\1/3\end{pmatrix},
\qquad f(s,a)=1-s+a.
\tag{2}
\]
The rows of \(A\) are indexed by \(s_2\in\{0,1\}\) and its columns by \(r_1\in\{0,1,2\}\). Notice that \(f(s,a)\in\{0,1,2\}\).

Here is the complete observed atom table. For every \(a_1,a_2\in\{0,1\}\), the only nonzero atoms have \(m_2=1\), \(y_2=f(s_2,a_2)\), and \(s_3=0\). Their masses are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
m_1&y_1&s_2&x_{a_1m_1y_1s_2a_2m_2y_2s_3}\\ \hline
1&0&0&1/48\\
1&1&0&1/48\\
1&1&1&1/24\\
1&2&1&1/48\\
0&0&0&1/16\\
0&0&1&1/12
\end{array}
\tag{3}
\]
and every atom not specified by this table is zero. Thus (3) lists every atom, including the zero cells by its last clause. For each fixed \((a_1,a_2)\), the displayed masses sum to
\[
\frac1{48}+\frac1{48}+\frac1{24}+\frac1{48}
+\frac1{16}+\frac1{12}=\frac14,
\]
so summing over the four action pairs proves normalization.

We next display the entire compatible full-law parameterization. For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), let \(0\leq\lambda_a\leq2\). For every \(a_1,a_2\), put \(r_2=f(s_2,a_2)\), \(m_2=1\), and \(s_3=0\). The only nonzero complete atoms are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
m_1&r_1&s_2&q_{a_1r_1m_1s_2a_2r_2m_2s_3}\\ \hline
1&0&0&1/48\\
1&1&0&1/48\\
1&1&1&1/24\\
1&2&1&1/48\\
0&0&0&(3-\lambda_{a_1})/48\\
0&1&0&\lambda_{a_1}/48\\
0&1&1&\lambda_{a_1}/24\\
0&2&1&(2-\lambda_{a_1})/24.
\end{array}
\tag{4}
\]
Every other complete atom is zero. Equation (4) is coefficient-expanded affine form: \(q^0\) is obtained by setting \(\lambda_0=\lambda_1=0\), and the column \(B_a\) is zero off \(A_1=a,M_1=0\) and has, for each \(a_2\), the four displayed coefficients \((-1/48,1/48,1/24,-1/24)\). Nonnegativity is equivalent to the four polynomial inequalities
\[
\lambda_0\geq0,\quad2-\lambda_0\geq0,quad
\lambda_1\geq0,\quad2-\lambda_1\geq0.
\tag{5}
\]
There are no other feasibility constraints.

We verify both directions of that last assertion. Marginalizing (4) over an erased \(R_1\) gives, for \(s_2=0\),
\[
\frac{3-\lambda_a}{48}+\frac{\lambda_a}{48}=\frac1{16},
\tag{6}
\]
and, for \(s_2=1\),
\[
\frac{\lambda_a}{24}+\frac{2-\lambda_a}{24}=\frac1{12}.
\tag{7}
\]
The respondent atoms are unchanged, so (6)--(7) prove \(O_\#q=p\). For fixed \((a_1,r_1,m_1,s_2)\), the two stage-two action cylinder masses in (4) are equal. Their sum is twice either mass, so (1) verifies the full-history logging equation at stage two. Each stage-one action has total mass \(1/2\), verifying the same equation at stage one. Thus the correction to \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}factorization}\), not the rejected observed-history marginal equation, is satisfied.

Put
\[
w(\lambda)=(3-\lambda,\lambda,4-2\lambda)^\top.
\tag{8}
\]
Direct multiplication gives
\[
Aw(\lambda)=\begin{pmatrix}
((3-\lambda)+\lambda)/12\\
\lambda/6+(4-2\lambda)/12
\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1/4\\1/3\end{pmatrix}=\boldsymbol\beta.
\tag{9}
\]
For each \((a_1,r_1)\), the stage-one respondent and nonrespondent \(S_2\)-vectors obtained by summing (4) over \(a_2\) are respectively \(A_{\cdot r_1}/2\) and \(A_{\cdot r_1}w_{r_1}(\lambda_{a_1})/2\). They are proportional, so every stage-one weak-shadow cross-product is zero on both sides, including zero cells. At stage two, every \(M_2=0\) cylinder has mass zero, so all stage-two cross-products also hold.

Conversely, let \(q\in\mathcal K(p)\). The zero observed cells in (3) force \(M_2=1\), \(R_2=f(S_2,A_2)\), and \(S_3=0\) almost surely and fix each respondent atom in (4). Full-history behavior factorization at stage two makes the two \(A_2\)-atom masses equal separately for every \((a_1,r_1,m_1,s_2)\). The stage-one cross-products then make the nonrespondent \(S_2\)-vector for each \((a_1,r_1)\) proportional to the nonzero respondent column \(A_{\cdot r_1}\). Therefore it has the form \(A_{\cdot r_1}w_{a_1,r_1}/2\) for a unique \(w_{a_1,r_1}\geq0\). Observed missing-cell marginalization is exactly
\[
Aw_{a_1}=\boldsymbol\beta.
\tag{10}
\]
Row reduction of (10) gives
\[
w_{a,0}+w_{a,1}=3,qquad 2w_{a,1}+w_{a,2}=4,
\tag{11}
\]
so, with \(\lambda_a=w_{a,1}\), (8) follows; nonnegativity gives precisely (5). This proves that (4)--(5), rather than merely a chosen subfamily, are the complete affine fiber.

For comparison with the signed-minor handle, all minors are
\[
D^{01}=\frac1{72},\qquad D^{02}=\frac1{144},\qquad
D^{12}=\frac1{144},
\tag{12}
\]
and hence
\[
z=(D^{12},-D^{02},D^{01})^\top
=\frac1{144}(1,-1,2)^\top,qquad
(-1,1,-2)^\top=-144z.
\tag{13}
\]
In particular \(D^{02}\ne0\), so \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=2\), and (13) spans its one-dimensional null space. The stage-one missing-reward coefficient row and the stage-two action-reward coefficient row are
\[
c^{(1)}=(0,1/4,1/6),
\qquad c^{(2)}=(x_0/12,x_1/4,x_2/12).
\tag{14}
\]
Cofactor expansion, here also checked by direct dot products, yields the complete continuation determinants
\[
G_1=c^{(1)}z=\frac1{1728},qquad
G_2=c^{(2)}z=\frac{x_0-3x_1+2x_2}{1728}.
\tag{15}
\]

Now take the deployment policy
\[
\pi_1(0\mid s_0)=1,qquad
\pi_2(1\mid h_2^F)=x_{R_1},qquad
\pi_2(0\mid h_2^F)=1-x_{R_1},
\tag{16}
\]
at every full history, with \(x\in(0,1)^3\). This is reward-history blind exactly on the diagonal \(x_0=x_1=x_2\). Because (1) is the actual action law conditional on full history, the importance ratios in \(\mathrm{def{:}stage\text{-}value}\) perform genuine change of policy. Since (16) assigns zero probability to \(A_1=1\), both stage values depend only on \(\lambda_0\), which we abbreviate as \(\lambda\).

The column totals of \(A\) are
\[
d=(1/12,1/4,1/12).
\tag{17}
\]
Using (8), the first-stage value is
\[
\ell_1(\lambda)=\sum_{r=0}^2r,d_r(1+w_r(\lambda))
=\frac{13}{12}-\frac{\lambda}{12}.
\tag{18}
\]
Also, the target-law probability of \(S_2=0\) is the respondent row mass \(1/6\) plus the missing mass \(1/4\), hence \(5/12\). Since \(R_2=1-S_2+A_2\), (16)--(17) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\ell_2(\lambda)
&=\frac5{12}+\sum_{r=0}^2d_r(1+w_r(\lambda))x_r\\
&=\frac5{12}+\frac{x_0}{3}+\frac{x_1}{4}+\frac{5x_2}{12}
+\lambda\left(-\frac{x_0}{12}+\frac{x_1}{4}-\frac{x_2}{6}\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
Define the coefficient-expanded slope polynomial
\[
M_7(x)=-x_0+3x_1-2x_2;
\tag{20}
\]
then the slope in (19) is \(g(x)=M_7(x)/12\). Equations (18)--(20) are the complete elimination of \((\lambda_0,\lambda_1)\) from the two pairs of stage-face systems. They imply
\[
\Delta^-(p)=\Delta^+(p)=
\begin{cases}
0,&M_7(x)\leq0,\\
2\min\{M_7(x)/12,1/12\},&M_7(x)>0.
\end{cases}
\tag{21}
\]
Indeed, if \(M_7\leq0\), both (18) and (19) are nonincreasing, so \(\lambda=2\) is a common minimizer and \(\lambda=0\) a common maximizer. If \(M_7>0\), their slopes have opposite signs. The rectangular lower value uses \((\lambda_1,\lambda_2)=(2,0)\), and the rectangular upper value uses \((0,2)\), whereas a common \(\lambda\) minimizes or maximizes the sum at one endpoint according to the sign of \(M_7/12-1/12\). Subtracting the corresponding affine endpoint values gives (21). This is also a direct verification of the face criterion in \(\mathrm{lem{:}compact\text{-}face\text{-}pasting}\).

For completeness, a coefficient-expanded strict sign dossier for this policy slice is
\[
\begin{array}{lll}
M_1=x_0,&M_2=1-x_0,&M_3=x_1,\\
M_4=1-x_1,&M_5=x_2,&M_6=1-x_2,\\
M_7=-x_0+3x_1-2x_2,
&M_8=(x_0-x_1)^2+(x_1-x_2)^2.&
\end{array}
\tag{22}
\]
The declared sign vector is \(M_j>0\) for \(1\leq j\leq8\). It defines a relatively open subset of the fixed-\((p,\mu)\) compatible policy slice, and (21) proves strict containment throughout it.

At the rational policy
\[
(x_0,x_1,x_2)=\left(\frac1{140},\frac{521}{980},\frac1{980}\right),
\tag{23}
\]
all action probabilities in (16) and their complements are positive, \(M_8>0\), and
\[
\frac{x_0}{3}+\frac{x_1}{4}+\frac{5x_2}{12}=\frac{19}{140},
\qquad g(x)=\frac{37}{280},
\qquad M_7(x)=\frac{111}{70}>0.
\tag{24}
\]
Thus (18)--(19) become
\[
\ell_1(\lambda)=\frac{13}{12}-\frac{\lambda}{12},
\qquad
\ell_2(\lambda)=\frac{58}{105}+\frac{37\lambda}{280}.
\tag{25}
\]
The total slope is \(41/840>0\). Consequently
\[
\Theta_I(p)=
\left[\frac{13}{12}+\frac{58}{105},
\frac{11}{12}+\frac{49}{60}\right]
=\left[\frac{229}{140},\frac{26}{15}\right].
\tag{26}
\]
The equality with the whole interval, not merely its endpoints, follows because the continuous affine map in \(\lambda\) sends \([0,2]\) onto that interval; \(\lambda_1\) is immaterial. Separately minimizing and maximizing (25) gives
\[
L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\frac{11}{12}+\frac{58}{105}
=\frac{617}{420},
\qquad
U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\frac{13}{12}+\frac{49}{60}
=\frac{19}{10},
\tag{27}
\]
and subtraction of (26) from (27) yields
\[
\Delta^-(p)=\Delta^+(p)=\frac16.
\tag{28}
\]
Equations (3)--(15) verify, cell by cell, normalization, observed marginalization, full-history behavior factors, positivity, every weak-shadow cross-product, \(Aw=\boldsymbol\beta\), the null directions, and the continuation determinants required for this exact witness.

It remains to prove the negative conclusion about the proposed equality variety. Fix the rational \((p,\mu)\) in (1)--(3) and let
\[
\mathcal U_-=\{x\in(0,1)^3:M_7(x)<0,\ M_8(x)>0\},
\qquad
\mathcal U_+=\{x\in(0,1)^3:M_7(x)>0,\ M_8(x)>0\}.
\tag{29}
\]
Both sets are nonempty and open: for example, points sufficiently near \((3/4,1/4,3/4)\) lie in \(\mathcal U_-\), while (23) lies in \(\mathcal U_+\). The rank minor in (12) is nonzero throughout this fixed-law slice, and \(M_8>0\) removes every reward-history-blind policy. By (21), every point of \(\mathcal U_-\) is an endpoint-equality point, whereas every point of \(\mathcal U_+\) is a strict-containment point.

Suppose, contrary to the requested conclusion, that a finite family of coefficient polynomials had a common-zero set equal to the equality locus after the stated rank and policy exceptions were removed. Restrict each polynomial to fixed \((p,\mu)\) and substitute the affine policy coordinates \((x_0,x_1,x_2,1-x_0,1-x_1,1-x_2)\). The result is a polynomial in \(x\) that vanishes on the open set \(\mathcal U_-\). Such a polynomial is identically zero: on an open box inside \(\mathcal U_-\), fix two coordinates and view it as a univariate polynomial in the third; infinitely many roots make every coefficient zero, and repeating this argument in the remaining coordinates makes every coefficient of the original polynomial zero. Hence every restricted polynomial also vanishes on \(\mathcal U_+\). That would classify the strict points in \(\mathcal U_+\) as equality points, contradicting (21).

Therefore the equality locus, even after removal of precisely the advertised rank-degenerate and reward-history-blind faces, is a semialgebraic region with interior rather than a common-zero algebraic variety. Requirement (vi) of \(\mathrm{oeq{:}generic\text{-}strict\text{-}containment}\) is false, so no dossier can satisfy all six requested properties. The exact computable replacement is the sign characterization (21): in this fully verified slice, a strict inequality, not a polynomial equality ideal, separates strict containment from rectangular equality.
theorem.justification: The exact rational slice verifies strict dynamic nonrectangularity under the corrected logger restriction and also gives an explicit generic-class certificate that the requested common-zero equality-locus theorem is mathematically false.
theorem.gap: Rectangular robust dynamic programs assume pasting. The exact slice computes the failure of pasting, but it also shows that rectangular equality occupies an open sign chamber rather than an exceptional algebraic variety.
theorem.consumer: An analyst can evaluate the printed slope polynomial to distinguish strict and rectangular chambers in the verified slice; the theorem also prevents an invalid equality-ideal diagnostic from being advertised.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(q\in\mathcal K(p)\), let \(q^\pi\) be the trajectory law obtained by retaining the initial-state law and every conditional kernel of \((R_t,M_t,S_{t+1})\) given \((H_t^F,A_t)\) from \(q\), while replacing the action kernel by \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid H_t^F)\). Under full-history behavior factorization and behavior positivity, \(q^\pi\ll q\) through every finite stage and
\[
\mathbb E_{q^\pi}[R_t]=\ell_t(q),\qquad
\mathbb E_{q^\pi}\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^H R_t\right]=V_\pi(q).
\]
Thus the value functional is related to the causal deployment law by finite-horizon change of measure; the equality is not a definition of an observed-law regression.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Because every alphabet and the horizon are finite, disintegrate \(q\) in chronological order. Write \(e_t(r,m,s'\mid h,a)\) for a version of the conditional law of \((R_t,M_t,S_{t+1})\) given \((H_t^F,A_t)=(h,a)\). On a zero-mass history choose this kernel arbitrarily. Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}factorization}\) and membership in \(\mathcal K(p)\) imply, on every positive full-history cell,
\[
q(A_t=a\mid H_t^F=h)=\mu_t(a\mid O_t(h)).
\tag{1}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}positivity}\) gives \(\mu_t(a\mid O_t(h))\geq\epsilon>0\). Therefore every action that can be chosen by \(\pi_t\) is in the behavior support at every reached history. Inductively, any partial trajectory having positive probability under the policy-replaced law also has positive probability under \(q\): the initial law and the kernels \(e_t\) are common, and each behavior action factor corresponding to a positive deployment action factor is strictly positive. Hence \(q^\pi\ll q\) through every stage.

For a complete prefix through \((R_t,M_t,S_{t+1})\), chronological factorization under \(q\) and \(q^\pi\), cancellation of the common initial and \(e_u\) factors, and (1) give
\[
\frac{q^\pi(s_1,a_1,r_1,m_1,\ldots,a_t,r_t,m_t,s_{t+1})}
{q(s_1,a_1,r_1,m_1,\ldots,a_t,r_t,m_t,s_{t+1})}
=\prod_{u=1}^t
\frac{\pi_u(a_u\mid h_u^F)}{\mu_u(a_u\mid O_u(h_u^F))}
=\rho_t^\pi.
\tag{2}
\]
All denominators in (2) are positive. Summing \(R_t\) times the left side of (2) against the corresponding \(q\)-prefix probabilities gives
\[
\mathbb E_{q^\pi}[R_t]
=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}q(\omega)\rho_t^\pi(\omega)R_t(\omega)
=\ell_t(q),
\tag{3}
\]
where the second equality is \(\mathrm{def{:}stage\text{-}value}\). Finally, the horizon is finite, so linearity of expectation and \(V_\pi(q)=\sum_{t=1}^H\ell_t(q)\) yield
\[
\mathbb E_{q^\pi}\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^H R_t\right]
=\sum_{t=1}^H\mathbb E_{q^\pi}[R_t]
=\sum_{t=1}^H\ell_t(q)=V_\pi(q).
\]
This proves the asserted relationship between the latent causal target and the compatible-law functional.
added_lemmas.justification: This closes the reviewer's change-of-policy objection by proving that the corrected full-history logger equation makes the frozen pi-over-mu functional equal the complete-information deployment value.
added_lemmas.gap: Observed-history action margins alone do not supply this likelihood ratio; the full-history conditional logging restriction does.
added_lemmas.consumer: Every sharp value and confidence-set result can now interpret the optimized full-law functional as the oracle deployment-policy value.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}p\), use the same fixed kernels \(\mu\) and \(\pi\) in every summand, and define the cutoff and \(C_{n,\alpha}\) as in \(\mathrm{def{:}confidence\text{-}fiber}\). Then
\[
\Pr_p\!\left\{\Theta_I(p)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}\right\}
\geq \Pr_p\!\left\{p\in C_{n,\alpha}\right\}
\geq 1-\alpha.
\]
The condition \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\) is needed only to make the covered identified set nonempty. The first inequality can be strict, so the confidence-fiber image is an exact finite-sample, possibly conservative, whole-set confidence region.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(E=\{p\in C_{n,\alpha}\}\) and \(F=\{\Theta_I(p)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}\}\). The proof uses event inclusion and the defining multinomial quantile; it does not identify the causal target by an observed regression.

On \(E\), if \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), then \(p\) is one of the indices in the union in \(\mathrm{def{:}whole\text{-}set\text{-}region}\). Hence its own summand occurs and
\[
\Theta_I(p)\subseteq
\bigcup_{\substack{p'\in C_{n,\alpha}\\\mathcal K(p')\ne\varnothing}}
\Theta_I(p')=\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}.
\tag{1}
\]
If instead \(\mathcal K(p)=\varnothing\), then \(\mathrm{def{:}identified\text{-}set}\) gives \(\Theta_I(p)=\varnothing\), and (1) is again true. Thus \(E\subseteq F\), which proves
\[
\Pr_p(F)\geq\Pr_p(E).
\tag{2}
\]

Under \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid\text{-}trajectories}\), \(n\widehat p_n\) has the multinomial distribution with parameters \((n,p)\). By \(\mathrm{def{:}confidence\text{-}fiber}\), the event \(E\) is
\[
2nD_{\mathrm{KL}}(\widehat p_n\Vert p)\leq c_{n,\alpha}(p).
\tag{3}
\]
The cutoff is a \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of the random variable on the left of (3) under that same multinomial law. By the defining property of a quantile, including possible atoms at the cutoff,
\[
\Pr_p(E)\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{4}
\]
Combining (2) and (4) proves the two inequalities. No equality between the two probabilities follows: values belonging to other laws in the random fiber can cover \(\Theta_I(p)\) even when \(p\notin C_{n,\alpha}\), which is the stated source of conservativeness.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the promised usable whole-set inference conclusion, rather than only a definition of a confidence-fiber image.
added_lemmas.gap: Pointwise inversion of a valid multinomial law confidence set yields simultaneous coverage of the entire true value image without selecting one latent completion.
added_lemmas.consumer: A finite-table OPE analysis can report the union image as an exact finite-sample, possibly conservative, confidence region for every value compatible with the true observed law.

proposed_core_edits.name: qfull

proposed.name: qfull
proposed.def: The cylinder marginal of \(q\) at \((H_t^F,A_t)=(h,a)\), with \(q_t^F(h)=\sum_{a'\in\mathcal A}q_t^F(h,a')\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The corrected logging restriction is a full-history cylinder equation and needs its own well-typed marginal rather than the observed-history marginal qobs.

proposed.condition: \(q_t^F(h,a)=\mu_t(a\mid O_t(h))\sum_{a'\in\mathcal A}q_t^F(h,a')\) for every \(t\in\mathcal T\), \(h\in\mathcal H_t^F\), and \(a\in\mathcal A\), where \(O_t(h)\in\mathcal H_t^O\) is the recorded-history coarsening of \(h\). Equivalently, on every positive full-history cell, \(q(A_t=a\mid H_t^F=h)=\mu_t(a\mid H_t^O=O_t(h))\); the displayed homogeneous equation is imposed also on zero-mass cells.

standard.name: Known recorded-history behavior policy conditional on complete history

proposed_core_edits.reason: Observed-history marginal factorization does not identify the action law conditional on latent reward history. The replacement states the design restriction that the logger uses recorded history and therefore makes the pi/mu change-of-policy ratio valid.

proposed.name: Full-history weak-shadow compatible-law fiber
proposed.construction:
\[
\mathcal K(p)=\left\{q\in\Delta(\Omega):
\begin{array}{ll}
O_\#q=p, & \\
q_t^F(h,a)=\mu_t(a\mid O_t(h))\displaystyle\sum_{a'\in\mathcal A}q_t^F(h,a')
&\forall (t,h,a)\in\mathcal T\times\mathcal H_t^F\times\mathcal A,\\
q_t(h,a,r,1,s)q_t(h,a,r,0,s')
=q_t(h,a,r,0,s)q_t(h,a,r,1,s')
&\forall (t,h,a,r,s,s')\in
\mathcal T\times\mathcal H_t^F\times\mathcal A\times\mathcal R\times\mathcal S^2
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
Here \(O_t:\mathcal H_t^F\to\mathcal H_t^O\) is the history-level restriction of the coarsening map \(O\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Compatibility must impose the corrected full-history behavior cylinders on every latent history cell; retaining only observed-history action margins would not justify policy reweighting.

proposed.name: Continuation-weighted stage value under full-history logging
proposed.construction:
For every \(t\in\mathcal T\),
\[
\ell_t(q)=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}q(\omega)\rho_t^\pi(\omega)R_t(\omega)
=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}q(\omega)
\left\{\prod_{u=1}^t
\frac{\pi_u(A_u(\omega)\mid H_u^F(\omega))}
{\mu_u(A_u(\omega)\mid O_u(H_u^F(\omega)))}\right\}R_t(\omega),
\]
where \(O_u(H_u^F(\omega))=H_u^O(\omega)\).

prose_updates.tldr: Finite-horizon MNAR policy value is the image of a compact full-history fiber only after the known recorded-history logger is imposed conditional on every complete latent history. An exact two-stage rational slice has sharp value image \([229/140,26/15]\), rectangular endpoints \(617/420\) and \(19/10\), and two endpoint gaps of \(1/6\). The same elimination refutes the proposed exceptional algebraic equality locus: rectangular equality and strict containment occupy opposite open policy sign chambers. Simultaneous multinomial confidence-fiber inversion covers the whole true identified set with finite-sample probability at least \(1-\alpha\), possibly conservatively.

project_justification.gap: Static weak-shadow programs do not determine whether latent reward completions that separately extremize different continuation values can be pasted into one dynamic law. Moreover, a known policy based on recorded history must be imposed conditional on complete history before the usual deployment-to-logging likelihood ratio is valid.
project_justification.niche: The exact two-stage slice supplies a cell-complete strict-containment certificate under the sound logging restriction and identifies a structural obstruction to the proposed equality-variety headline: equality is an inequality-defined chamber with nonempty interior, not merely a lower-dimensional collision set.
project_justification.fill: The note reports the exact affine completion, signed minors, continuation slopes, rational sharp and rectangular endpoints, and sign-chamber characterization. It replaces the impossible common-zero equality-locus promise by the proved semialgebraic chamber result and adds an exact finite-sample whole-set coverage theorem.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling of complete recorded trajectories from a finite-horizon behavior process whose action kernel is known and uses only recorded history.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent recorded trajectories, each contributing one multinomial cell in \(\mathcal O\).
sampling_model.treatment: For every complete history \(h\), the conditional behavior action law is \(\mu_t(\cdot\mid O_t(h))\); thus latent rewards do not influence logging beyond their recorded coarsening. The fixed deployment rule \(\pi\) may use latent rewards and is therefore an oracle policy unless a reward-recovery or sensing mechanism is supplied.
sampling_model.overlap: The known kernel satisfies \(\mu_t(a\mid O_t(h))\ge\epsilon>0\) for every complete-history/action cell, so each deployment-to-logging ratio is finite.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The observed multinomial law is inverted jointly. Fixed-law value images and face systems are certified by global real-algebraic optimization; the exact multinomial confidence fiber itself is used through its defining likelihood-ratio inequality and need not be encoded as a polynomial set.

prose_updates.related_work: Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong's static weak-shadow program remains the one-stage benchmark. Iyengar's finite-horizon robust Bellman recursion assumes rectangular ambiguity, whereas the exact two-stage table here proves that the inverse observed-data fiber need not permit simultaneous stagewise extrema. The stronger proposed claim that equality is confined to an algebraic collision variety is false: the verified policy slice has an open equality chamber and an open strict chamber. Wang, Xu, Lu, and Song's response-model inverse-weighting workflow and Wei, Qu, and Miao's bridge/completeness workflow can be reanalysed against these bounds only after their action mechanism is aligned with the corrected full-history logging equation; their additional point-identifying restrictions should be reported separately rather than built into the partial-identification target. Chen, Christensen, and Tamer motivate confidence-set inversion, while the finite-sample theorem here proves whole-set coverage directly by inclusion of the true-law summand.
prose_updates.interpretation: In the verified two-stage design, compute \(M_7=-x_0+3x_1-2x_2\) from the oracle policy's reward-specific second-stage action probabilities. If \(M_7>0\), the first- and second-stage programs select opposite completion faces and both rectangular endpoints are too wide; if \(M_7\le0\), they share extremizers and the rectangular endpoints are exact. This diagnostic is exact for the printed rational slice, not a universal polynomial ideal for all two-stage tables.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact sign characterization is proved on the displayed fixed-observed-law, fixed-logger policy slice. It does not establish that one sign vector is relatively open in the entire space of all compatible two-stage observed laws. More importantly, the requested global common-zero equality variety cannot exist because the slice already contains a full-dimensional open equality chamber away from rank degeneracy and reward-history blindness. A complete-information deployment policy remains operationally unavailable without reward recovery, and confidence-fiber coverage can be conservative.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The corrected model imposes the recorded-history behavior kernel conditional on every complete history; under that restriction the pi-over-mu functional is the deployment-policy value. The exact table proof verifies every observed and complete atom, normalization, full-history behavior equations, positivity, weak-shadow cross-products, affine feasibility box, signed minors, continuation determinants, sharp image, rectangular endpoints, and strict gaps. It also proves a negative result: no finite common-zero polynomial family can characterize all equality points after only the advertised rank and policy exceptions are removed. Accordingly, no field-tier generic equality-variety claim is made. The whole-set confidence region has exact finite-sample coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) for the entire true identified set, with model compatibility needed only for nonvacuity.
